diffuseAlbedo.note: A first colour for Bath stone (Monks Park, oolitic limestone): no measured colour was read: a first value read from trade and museum photographs of the named material.

refractiveIndex.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.specularF0 (0.0533, calcite grains in random orientations)
refractiveIndex.derivation: n = (1 + sqrt(F0)) / (1 - sqrt(F0)), the index whose normal-incidence reflectance is the record's F0

porosity.source: BRE (Building Research Establishment), 'Monks Park Limestone: Technical Data Sheet', Monks Park Mine, Corsham, Wilts, compiled September 1997 (tests at BRE 1996; porosity method Note 3 = prEN 1341 / BRE 141), Test Results table, 'Porosity and Water Absorption', pp. 3-4, https://bregroup.com/documents/311572/1309416/Monks+Park+Limestone.pdf/031955ac-5182-4710-370d-33f40c2466b2
porosity.note: Verified on the sheet. Porosity 23.8 % is on p. 3. The saturation coefficient of 0.85, the water absorption of 10.3 % by weight and the bulk density of 2066 kg/m3 (labelled 'bulk specific gravity') are on p. 4, not p. 3. The sheet calls the stone 'a fine-grained, buff coloured stone' and an oolitic limestone of the Great Oolite. It says three beds tested earlier had similar porosity and water absorption.

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.note: Its ooids, the sand-sized spheres an oolite is built of (under 2 mm by definition).

bed.source: MuseeVision/Docs/Stages/albion.md §3.1 Coursing (BandCuts): 'every 1.20 one red course of 0.30 and three buff of 0.30'; §3.10 maps albion.wall.buff to accent.bath-stone
bed.note: Verified in albion.md lines 119-122 and 322. The value is the height of the designed buff ashlar course, not a natural bed, and 'design' is the honest grade. BRE's Monks Park sheet (p. 2) says the stone is worked in galleries about 6 m high and seems to be divided into 'four or more beds'. A 0.30 m block therefore shows no natural bed.

bedAspect.note: How much longer the structure runs along its bedding than across it.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
